whyThisMatters: If you can name the trick out loud together, you will spot it faster on your own — whether it shows up in a permit request, a vendor invoice, or a tracking alert. Today's riddles use the same patterns Operations sees every day.
rememberThis: This month gave these tricks a name — keep using them. STOP before you skip a sign-off or approve a change, VERIFY through your own known channel, then REPORT.

discussionPrompts: Ask which two terms are easiest to mix up — FAKE INTERNAL TOOL ALERT and AUTHORITY IMPERSONATION both attach a deadline or a fee to an otherwise calm, official-looking notice, but the source they copy is different.
Ask for a real example of an internal alert or vendor invoice that matches one of these terms.
Ask someone to explain SAFETY SIGN-OFF BYPASS in their own words, without using the term itself.

Ask which two terms are easiest to mix up now — INSURANCE CLAIM ADVANCE-FEE FRAUD and VENDOR BANK-DETAIL CHANGE both involve a payment-related ask, but one is tied to a pending claim and the other to an existing vendor invoice.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: People most often mix up FAKE INTERNAL TOOL ALERT and AUTHORITY IMPERSONATION. Both look calm and routine on the surface, so people pick one when the riddle points to the other. The difference: a fake tool alert copies your own company's system; authority impersonation copies an outside official body like a port authority.

riddles.riddle: I say the supervisor is unreachable and ask you to skip the signed permit-to-work "just this once". What trick am I?
I am a dry-dock invoice with updated bank details, and I ask you to use them for this payment and every one after. What trick am I?
I look exactly like your fleet-tracking tool's own alert, and I ask you to verify your session through my link within 5 minutes. What trick am I?
I claim to be a port authority asking you to settle a deficiency fee to keep clearance on schedule, but I didn't come through your own PSC liaison. What trick am I?
I ask you to update the vessel's discharge port and cargo instructions, with no signed addendum. What trick am I?
I am the three-step habit: 1. STOP before you act, 2. VERIFY using a number or portal you already trust, 3. REPORT to the IT Service Desk. What is this rule called?
I claim your crew's flight was cancelled and ask for a rebooking fee paid to a new account before the change date. What trick am I?
I claim to be your P&I Club or claims handler and ask for an upfront processing fee before releasing a pending claim payout. What trick am I?
I look like your weather-routing service's own advisory, but I arrive as an urgent email attachment instead of through the portal, recommending a costly course change. What trick am I?
